subject: PrivPlan entitlement & invoice exception for MedLink Health
messages:
From: Alyssa Martin <alyssa@medlink.io>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medlink.io
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivPlan entitlement & invoice exception for MedLink Health

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks again for walking us through the Azure Private Plan yesterday. Procurement has one sticky point before we can sign: their finance team insists the invoice needs to be split across two internal cost centers (SOW line 1 = platform, SOW line 2 = professional services) and routed to our reseller (MidCorp) for pass-through billing. Azure Private Plans normally invoice through the Marketplace merchant flow and don't support a split on a single purchase order.

Is there a commercial or billing exception Redwood can make for MedLink so the invoice reflects both SOW lines and shows MidCorp as the reseller intermediary? We are happy to provide the PO and accept an interim process while Azure-side entitlement mapping is being worked out.

Attaching our PO template to show the fields procurement will require.

Attachments: MedLink_PO_Template.pdf

Appreciate a quick read — our target go-live is 05/10 and procurement wants this resolved before signature.

Best,
Alyssa Martin
Director, Strategic Procurement
MedLink Health

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Martin <alyssa@medlink.io>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivPlan entitlement & invoice exception for MedLink Health

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clarity.

Quick answer: we can usually accommodate a temporary invoicing approach to unblock a go-live, but there are two threads we need to close first: (1) legal redlines for the Private Plan amendment (data/residency/indemnity), and (2) the billing path for the reseller split. I’ve looped in Marissa (commercials) and Irene (legal) to propose options.

Can we do a 30-minute call today at 11:00 PT to align on the PO fields and confirm whether MidCorp can be listed as reseller on Redwood's invoice while Marketplace credits flow later? If that works, Marissa will follow with the entitlement mapping and Ben from billing will join to confirm the reconciliation process.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed entitlement map + temporary invoice flow

Hi Alyssa — great to connect this morning. Following up with the commercial approach we discussed on the call:

- Entitlement mapping: Redwood can create two SKUs in the Private Plan that map to your SOW lines; one SKU for "Platform Runtime" and one SKU for "Professional Services Credits." The Private Plan purchase can include both SKUs so Azure will provision entitlements accordingly. I have attached a proposed entitlement map showing how token/seat assignments map to your internal cost centers.

- Temporary invoice flow: to unblock you we can issue a Redwood invoice directly to MedLink with MidCorp listed as the reseller on the invoice. Redwood will then reconcile with Azure Marketplace billing (merchant credits) in the subsequent invoice cycle. This is a short-term operational workaround; final state would be the Azure marketplace reflecting the reseller pass-through.

Open items we need from you: PO number, billing contact, and confirmation that MidCorp is authorized as your reseller intermediary. Once we have that Ben will confirm the reconciliation timeline.

Attachments: Proposed-Entitlement-Map.xlsx, Marketplace-Invoice-Flow.png

If that all sounds ok I’ll get legal to circulate the Private Plan amendment with the redlines Irene will request.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Martin <alyssa@medlink.io>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor Blake <connor.blake@medlink.io>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Private Plan amendment (initial redlines)

Alyssa / Team — attaching our initial redlines for the Private Plan amendment. High level comments:

1) Data residency & processing: we can confirm the Private Plan will honor regional residency requests, but need to include the specific region (US-East) in the amendment and an SLA for data export requests.
2) Indemnity cap: procurement asked to shift liability — we can accept a limited carve for breach of data obligations, but cannot remove the overall commercial cap.
3) DPA / subprocessors: your standard DPA is OK; please provide the contact for your privacy team so we can align on subprocessor notices.
4) Audit rights & evidence: for marketplace-delivered services we can provide attestation but full on-site audits require a separate statement of work.

I’ve uploaded the redlines as a Word doc. If Connor (your counsel) can indicate which items are deal breakers, we’ll prepare a DocuSign amendment for signature.

Attachments: Azure_PrivatePlan_Redlines.docx
Related link: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-privplan-amend

Regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:57:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivPlan entitlement & invoice exception for MedLink Health — billing details

Alyssa — quick billing note to make the operational path clear:

- If you want Redwood to invoice MedLink directly (with MidCorp shown as reseller), we will need the PO number and the legal billing name exactly as it should appear on the invoice.
- We will issue the invoice to MedLink, process payment, and then apply a marketplace credit reconciliation in the following 30-day billing cycle so your ledger nets out correctly. That typically takes 1–2 billing cycles to fully reconcile.
- To expedite onboarding, please complete the short billing checklist attached and provide the AP contact.

If procurement is uncomfortable with Redwood invoicing directly long-term, we can continue to pursue the Azure merchant flow as the final state. This temporary path is purely to unblock the go-live.

Attachments: Billing-Onboarding-Checklist.pdf

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this is helpful. Procurement has approved an interim process provided we get the following:

- PO number: ML-PO-7783 (attached filled PO)
- AP contact: ap@medlink.io / Mary Delgado
- Confirmation that Redwood will include MidCorp as the reseller on the invoice; procurement needs that field populated for vendor reconciliation.
- One final ask from procurement: a written SLA credit commitment for uptime greater than 99.5% during the first 6 months or a pro-rated credit. Is that something Redwood can commit to in the amendment?

Connor: we'll review Irene's redlines today and aim to sign as soon as counsel confirms the indemnity language. Once legal signs off we can complete DocuSign and proceed to procurement signature.

Attachments: ML-PO-7783.pdf

Alyssa Martin
Director, Strategic Procurement
MedLink Health
